item.title: El verdadero escándalo de Nvidia no es el que todos están mirando
item.description: Se presume que los reguladores del gobierno son árbitros neutrales, sin embargo, las relaciones personales y financieras con una empresa específica, en especial una tan grande e importante como Nvidia ...
item.dc:creator: Scott Lincicome
item.content:encoded: En los últimos días, la mayor parte de la información sobre Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ) se ha centrado en las supuestas relaciones extramatrimoniales de su exCEO Jensen Huang, los vínculos entre Nvidia y la administración del presidente Donald Trump, y cómo estos enredos podrían haber afectado a las ventas de semiconductores avanzados a China y, por ende, a la seguridad nacional de EE.UU. Son todas preguntas válidas. De acuerdo con diversos informes, la familia y la antigua empresa de inversiones del secretario de Comercio, Howard Lutnick, quien intervino para facilitar las exportaciones de los chips avanzados de Nvidia, en contra de la opinión de otros funcionarios de la administración Trump, tenían importantes inversiones tanto en la compañía como en los centros de datos del sudeste de Asia que usan tecnología de Nvidia y que podrían haber contribuido a las ambiciones de China en materia de inteligencia artificial. Huang, por su parte, mantenía una cercana relación con Trump, quien se hizo con un gran número de acciones de Nvidia apenas una semana antes de que su administración flexibilizara las normas de exportación relativas a los chips H200 de Nvidia. Para finales de agosto, la participación de Trump en Nvidia podría haber superado los US$60 millones. Queda por ver si estos puntos se relacionan entre sí, aunque los motivos de sospecha son evidentes y comprensibles. Se presume que los reguladores del gobierno son árbitros neutrales, sin embargo, las relaciones personales y financieras con una empresa específica, en especial una tan grande e importante como Nvidia, generan conflictos que podrían influir en sus decisiones. La influencia actúa en ambos sentidos: los ejecutivos con conexiones políticas ejercen presión para obtener subvenciones, una aplicación laxa de la normativa u otros favores estatales, al tiempo que los funcionarios parciales presionan a las compañías para que actúen por motivos personales o políticos en lugar de comerciales. En el caso de Nvidia, existen evidencias de que ambas cosas estaban ocurriendo. Curiosamente, hay otra parte de la saga de Nvidia que plantea problemas similares, aunque ha recibido mucha menos atención: la retención por parte del Gobierno de EE.UU. de una parte de los ingresos de Nvidia procedentes de China. En agosto del año pasado, el presidente anunció que Nvidia y Advanced Micro Devicer ( AMD ) pagarían al Gobierno el 15% de las ventas de determinados chips de IA a China, un acuerdo que, según Trump, había sido idea suya. En diciembre, el presidente anunció una reducción del 25% de las ventas del modelo H200 de Nvidia a China, que el Gobierno aplicó de forma ingeniosa mediante un decreto de en enero que, para evitar la prohibición constitucional de los impuestos a la exportación, imponía un arancel del 25% a los chips importados de Taiwán y reexportados a China. Al comparar las estimaciones federales de los aranceles pagados por las importaciones de los chips en cuestión con las reexportaciones de EE.UU. de esos mismos productos a China, Hong Kong y Macao, es posible calcular cuánto dinero le reportó este plan al Tío Sam: hasta US$333 millones hasta septiembre de 2026, lo cual no es ni una cantidad insignificante ni un cambio radical en las finanzas públicas. Cabe preguntarse si este dinero, y el acuerdo en general, influyeron en la decisión del Gobierno de aprobar las ventas de Nvidia a China o de ofrecer a la compañía otro trato especial, pero eso (casi) no viene al caso. El problema más grave es que el acuerdo inclina de forma inadecuada la balanza reguladora hacia un lado, y en este caso el sesgo forma parte de la política oficial del Gobierno de EE.UU. Los reguladores que deben decidir si la venta de chips al extranjero supone una amenaza para la seguridad nacional no deberían estar autorizados a cobrar una comisión por hacerlo. Este problema político no se limita a Nvidia y al esquema de licencias de exportación. Según el panel de control de propiedad gubernamental del Instituto Cato, desde junio de 2025 el gobierno de Estados Unidos ha firmado acuerdos de participación accionaria con 41 empresas, 27 de las cuales fueron financiadas por el Departamento de Comercio. Al menos dos de estos acuerdos involucran a compañías vinculadas a la administración Trump: el paquete de US$1.600 millones del Departamento de Comercio para USA Rare Earth depende de una recaudación de capital privado de US$1.500 millones por parte de la antigua firma de Lutnick, Cantor Fitzgerald. Al mismo tiempo el fabricante de imanes Vulcan Elements, que tiene acuerdos tanto con el Departamento de Comercio como con el Pentágono, está vinculado a 1789 Capital, la firma de capital de riesgo asociada con Donald Trump Jr. Al margen de las conexiones personales, estos planes de participación accionarial sin precedentes plantean conflictos similares a los que se observan en el caso de Nvidia, porque otorgan a Washington un interés financiero directo en las compañías objetivo y, en consecuencia, distorsionan tanto las decisiones corporativas como las del Gobierno. Cuando el Tío Sam deja de ser árbitro y se convierte en jugador, los conflictos son inevitables. Y surgirán nuevas sospechas siempre que el Gobierno interactúe con una de las compañías de su cada vez mayor cartera. Consideremos algunos ejemplos recientes. Meses después de que el Pentágono adquiriera una participación de US$1.000 millones en la división de misiles de L3Harris, la empresa matriz ganó un contrato con la FAA (por sus siglas en inglés, Administración Federal de Aviación) para modernizar la red de control de tráfico aéreo (¡vaya sorpresa!). Dos meses después, el Ejército seleccionó a Vulcan para suministrar imanes de tierras raras para su programa de drones SkyFoundry, el décimo contrato de defensa de la joven compañía. Y la empresa Intel ( INTC ), respaldada por el gobierno, acaba de recibir una exención de un año de la reciente prohibición de la FCC (por sus siglas en inlgés Comisión Federal de Comunicaciones) sobre robots industriales de fabricación extranjera. Estas y otras transacciones no son necesariamente impropias ni corruptas. (Otras empresas, por ejemplo, también han recibido exenciones de la FCC). No obstante, el riesgo de decisiones sesgadas es evidente, y las investigaciones del Congreso son esperadas y justificadas. La única forma de limitar estos problemas es poniendo fin a estas relaciones y restableciendo la separación entre los sectores público y privado de EE.UU., una separación que ha sustentado la libre empresa estadounidense durante décadas. Con el fin de recuperar su neutralidad regulatoria, el Gobierno debería desinvertir inmediatamente en sus participaciones accionarias corporativas y poner fin a esquemas similares, incluyendo la “acción dorada” de US Steel, los acuerdos de reparto de ingresos de Nvidia y AMD, y la nueva iniciativa del gobierno para codificar “campeones nacionales” (incluida Nvidia). El Congreso además debería endurecer las restricciones a las inversiones de altos funcionarios del gobierno, sus familias y sus antiguas compañías, y debería exigir mucha más transparencia sobre las posiciones de inversión que siguen siendo legales. Sin embargo, la verdadera solución consiste en reducir la influencia del Gobierno sobre la economía. “Cuando la compraventa está controlada por la legislación”, advirtió en su famosa frase el satírico P.J. O’Rourke, “lo primero que se compra y se vende son los legisladores”. Si sustituimos eso por la discrecionalidad del Ejecutivo y los acuerdos entre bastidores, el resultado es el lío de Nvidia y quizá también otros líos. Nada de esto implica la ausencia total de regulación; salvaguardar la seguridad nacional es una función propia del gobierno. Sin embargo, incluso en estos casos, como en el de los controles de exportación estadounidenses, existen sólidos argumentos para limitar la intervención gubernamental a los asuntos más graves, a fin de maximizar la eficacia y minimizar las consecuencias económicas y políticas negativas de las medidas. Toda regulación, ya sea relacionada con la seguridad o no, debe ser estrictamente necesaria, objetiva y estar libre de las lagunas legales que convierten las políticas bien intencionadas en instrumentos para el enriquecimiento personal. Puede que hoy el foco de atención recaiga sobre Nvidia y los controles de exportación de los Estados Unidos. Sin embargo, el corporativismo sin precedentes de la Administración Trump garantiza prácticamente que se avecinen todavía más problemas. Esta nota no refleja necesariamente la opinión del consejo editorial de Bloomberg LP y sus propietarios. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

Google picks Bezos' Blue Origin to launch AI computing satellites in 2029

FILE PHOTO: A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket is prepared for launch at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Cape Canaveral, Florida, U.S., April 18, 2026. REUTERS/Joe Skipper/File Photo

FAST

Nov 19 : Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin said on Thursday that Alphabet's Google had selected its New Glenn rocket to launch satellites for Project Suncatcher, an experiment aimed at running AI systems in space. The planned mission advances efforts to move power-hungry AI computing beyond Earth, using sunlight in orbit to ease pressure on electricity grids, land and cooling systems. Companies including Elon Musk's SpaceX and startup Starcloud are exploring data centers in orbit as growing AI use drives demand for computing capacity and strains infrastructure supporting facilities on the ground. The launch, targeted for the first quarter of 2029, will be Google's first heavy-lift flight dedicated to Project Suncatcher and will carry several computing satellites aboard New Glenn.

Each satellite will carry Google's tensor processing units, the search giant's in-house chips built to run AI programs, with computing capacity roughly equal to a rack of servers in a conventional data center. They will enter an orbit that provides near-continuous sunlight, allowing Google to examine whether solar energy can support intensive computing in space. Thursday's agreement gives Blue Origin a major future mission for New Glenn as the company seeks to expand its launch business following delays and a launchpad explosion in May. Google and Planet Labs launched the first Project Suncatcher prototype aboard a SpaceX rocket in October and said the satellite was operating as expected after establishing contact. That mission is testing whether the chips can withstand launch forces, radiation and extreme temperatures, while engineers study how to cool them without the airflow available on Earth. Radiation can damage electronics and corrupt data, while heat from powerful chips must be released through pipes and panels rather than conventional cooling systems. Experts have also noted that high launch costs, engineering hurdles and limited satellite production can put data centers in orbit years away from commercial use.

Source: Reuters

Violence rises in Bangladesh as Hasina supporters escalate protests, PM Rahman blames India

By Zia Chowdhury and Hritam Mukherjee DHAKA, Nov 19 (Reuters) – Fresh violence broke out in Bangladesh on Thursday as former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s supporters tried to bring businesses and public transport to a halt, with mixed success, and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman blamed India for the unrest.

Unrelated protests by garment workers demanding higher wages also continued in some districts, with hundreds of workers blocking a highway into the capital Dhaka, forcing factories to close.

The rising unrest in the Muslim-majority nation of 175 million people — the world’s second-biggest garment exporter after China — threatens the fragile stability established since elections this year brought Rahman, a political opponent of Hasina’s outlawed Awami League, to power.

Show Full Article

Tensions have risen since Hasina, who fled after a student uprising against her rule in August 2024 and lives in exile in India, said she planned to return in December.

The Awami League called Thursday’s nationwide lockdown at the end of a week-long campaign of protests and rallies against the government’s rejection of her request for a new passport that would allow her to return. The attempted shutdown was successful mostly in the southern districts where the League is strongest.

Rahman’s government has accused Awami League leaders outside Bangladesh of fanning the violence and vowed action. Awami League leaders, most of them in hiding, could not be reached for comment.

PM RAHMAN POINTS FINGER AT ‘COUNTRY ACROSS BORDER’

At a public event in the northern district of Lalmonirhat, Rahman said Awami League leaders “have not looked at the interests of Bangladesh and its people”.

“At the same time, the country across the border, where they have fled to, is their master … To satisfy those masters, they have again started conspiring against Bangladesh, and its people,” he said, without naming India.

The Indian foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

After Hasina was ousted, relations with India deteriorated sharply under the interim government of Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus in Dhaka.

Ties have improved slightly since Rahman took office in February, although tensions over Hasina’s continued presence in India remain a major irritant.

Police said two members of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party had been killed on Wednesday night, while the houses of two BNP lawmakers in Hasina’s home district of Gopalganj were vandalised and set alight.

Awami League supporters also attacked some markets and vandalised some shops in Gopalganj town, they said.

At least six buses and pickup vans were set on fire along with a section of railway line, and crude bomb blasts were reported across six districts overnight. A bus and a truck were set on fire on Thursday on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway, police said, adding that the bus passengers had escaped unharmed.

YUNUS’ HOME SET ABLAZE

To deter violence, 97 platoons of the paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh have fanned out across seven districts, including Gopalganj and Faridpur, considered to have many Hasina supporters, a Guard spokesperson said.

In Dhaka, police arrested 107 people suspected of links to the Awami League and its affiliated organisations in the space of 24 hours, including former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid, police said.

Yunus’ ancestral home in the port city of Chattogram, about 300 km (185 miles) southeast of Dhaka, was set on fire late on Wednesday.

It was likely that flammable substances had been thrown into an unused ground-floor room, police officer Mozammel Haque said. He said Yunus’ paternal family members, who live on the upper floors, were safe.

Reuters could not immediately reach the Yunus Centre think tank, which speaks on his behalf.

(Reporting by Zia Chowdhury in Dhaka; Additional reporting by Hritam Mukherjee; Writing by Tanvi Mehta and YP Rajesh; Editing by Clarence Fernandez, Sharon Singleton and Editing by Kevin Liffey)

Explainer-Rohingya crisis remains unresolved as ICJ rules on Myanmar

Reuters

19 November, 2026 07:00 pm IST

Follow Us:

-->

Nov 19 (Reuters) – A long-awaited judgment from the UN’s highest court on Thursday said that killings, destruction of homes and widespread sexual violence by Myanmar’s security forces amounted to state-sponsored genocide of the Rohingya Muslim minority population.

The decision comes nearly a decade after a 2017 military crackdown drove more than 730,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh, and as conflict, shrinking humanitarian aid and dangerous sea crossings continue to leave many members of the community displaced and vulnerable.

WHY DID THE ROHINGYA FLEE MYANMAR?

Show Full Article

More than 1.3 million Rohingya remain displaced across South and Southeast Asia, including 1.2 million in sprawling refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar in Bangladesh, according to the United Nations.

The largest displacement began in August 2017, when Myanmar’s armed forces launched an offensive following attacks by the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army insurgent group on about 30 police posts and an army base.

The military crackdown forced hundreds of thousands of Rohingya to flee into Bangladesh. Refugees described mass killings, gang rapes, torture and the burning of hundreds of villages, according to Human Rights Watch.

Myanmar’s government denied the allegations, saying its forces were targeting militants.

WHAT IS THE ICJ CASE AGAINST MYANMAR?

In 2019, Gambia filed a case at the International Court of Justice (ICJ), also known as the World Court, backed by the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, alleging that Myanmar’s 2017 military offensive in Rakhine State amounted to genocide.

The ICJ judgments are final and binding, but the court has limited means of enforcement and cannot convict individuals or issue arrest warrants.

In 2019 preliminary hearings in the ICJ case, Myanmar’s then leader, Aung San Suu Kyi, rejected Gambia’s accusations of genocide as “incomplete and misleading”.

The ICJ in January 2020 ordered Myanmar to take urgent measures to protect Rohingya people remaining in the country, including preventing possible genocidal acts and preserving evidence.

WHAT IS THE SITUATION IN RAKHINE?

Myanmar’s military, led by Min Aung Hlaing, seized power in February 2021. The overthrow of Aung San Suu Kyi’s elected government triggered a nationwide civil war that has killed an estimated 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million.

As conflict spread, renewed fighting between Myanmar’s military junta and the Arakan Army rebel group broke out in Rakhine State in November 2023, forcing more Rohingya civilians to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh.

The minority group has also faced attacks by the Arakan Army, which set alight swathes of the Rohingya settlement of Buthidaung in May 2024, Reuters has reported.

WHY CAN’T THE ROHINGYA RETURN?

As conflict rages on in Rakhine, conditions for the safe return of Rohingya refugees do not currently exist, according to aid groups.

Myanmar said in August that it had verified 308,797 people living in displacement camps in Bangladesh as former residents of Rakhine State, but repatriation would begin only when security conditions in Rakhine improve.

Some Rohingya refugees say they are not willing to go back without full rights, dignity, and citizenship.

Myanmar’s government has long seen the Rohingya as illegal migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh and denied them citizenship, even though Rohingya families have lived in Myanmar for generations.

Earlier repatriation plans in 2018 and 2019 resulted in no returns.

(Reporting by Reuters staff; Editing by Raju Gopalakrishnan)

Somalia orders UAE ambassador to leave, citing 'invasion'

"Measures will be taken against anyone who cooperates with UAE in the invasion against Somalia," Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud said in a broadcast on the state-run news agency on Thursday (Nov 19).

Soldiers with their armored vehicles near a checkpoint in Mogadishu. The UAE has helped fund and train Somalia's military and backed ports and other commercial ventures. (AP Photo/Farah Abdi Warsameh, File)

MOGADISHU: Somalia ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador on Thursday (Nov 19) to leave the country within 72 hours and withdrew its own envoy from Abu Dhabi, accusing the Emirates of unspecified violations of Somalia's sovereignty that amounted to an "open invasion". "Measures will be taken against anyone who cooperates with UAE in the invasion against Somalia," Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud said in a broadcast on the state-run news agency. "All Somalis are urged to defend their country and unite against the open invasion of the UAE against the sovereignty, security, land and unity of Somalis." The minister did not elaborate on the actions the UAE had taken that had provoked Somalia's response.

In a speech on Tuesday, Somalia's President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud had accused the UAE of giving economic and political support to some regional Somali governments to oppose the federal government. There was no immediate response from the UAE foreign ministry. The UAE, which has helped fund and train Somalia's military in the past and has backed ports and other commercial ventures there, has long denied meddling in the country's affairs.

Related:

UAE investigators say flydubai co-pilot was planning 'terrorist act'

In January, Somalia said it had ended all agreements with the UAE, including port deals and defence and security cooperation, accusing the UAE of undermining its national sovereignty. Three self-governing Somali regions that have close relations with the United Arab Emirates dismissed that move at the time. The UAE has long leveraged its wealth to expand its influence across the Horn of Africa, using a mix of economic, military and diplomatic clout to assert regional power. For decades Somalia's federal government has had only limited authority across the country, and has failed to defeat Islamist militants, despite years of international support, including African peacekeepers and US air strikes. The UAE trained hundreds of Somali troops from 2014 to 2018, and still covers salaries and provides logistics for around 3,400 Somali military police and special forces troops in and around the capital, according to senior Somali sources. It has also forged bonds directly with regional governments, committing hundreds of millions of dollars to ports and military infrastructure on the coast along global shipping routes.

Source: Reuters/ht

West presses Iran at IAEA to let inspections resume at bombed nuclear sites

Reuters

19 November, 2026 06:30 pm IST

Follow Us:

-->

Facebook

X

LinkedIn

WhatsApp

Email

Copy Link

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Stay updated with ThePrint:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

-->

By Francois Murphy VIENNA, Nov 19 (Reuters) – The United States, Britain, France and Germany jointly pressed Tehran at a meeting of the UN atomic watchdog’s board on Thursday to let inspectors return to its nuclear sites bombed by the US and Israel last year, accusing Tehran of “stonewalling”.

Iran has not granted the International Atomic Energy Agency access to those nuclear facilities since the military strikes against them in June 2025.

While the strikes destroyed or badly damaged Iran’s three uranium-enrichment plants known to have been operational at the time, Tehran has not said what happened to its stock of highly enriched uranium, which included material close to weapons grade and remains unaccounted for.

Show Full Article

“It should be of concern to all Members of this Board that for a year and a half, the Agency has lost continuity of knowledge regarding Iran’s previously verified stockpile of high-enriched uranium,” the four Western powers said in a joint statement to the IAEA’s 35-nation Board of Governors.

The board is holding a quarterly meeting this week. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi informed it that the only inspections in the last quarter were at the undamaged Bushehr nuclear power plant.

“The DG has repeatedly made clear that there is no current technical reason preventing the Agency from accessing the affected nuclear facilities and that inspectors have been ready to return for a long time now,” the four countries said.

“It is up to Iran to seize this opportunity, change course, and address the international community’s long-standing concerns regarding its nuclear program,” they added, referring to “Iran’s stonewalling strategy”.

The US and Israel have not launched major strikes on Iranian nuclear sites since their 12-day campaign last year, but the US has been at war with Iran for nine months and speculation about fresh strikes is mounting while talks on a negotiated solution are deadlocked.

Iran says the US and Israeli attacks caused the current standoff over inspections.

“The root causes of the impossibility of normal safeguards implementation in Iran are the acts of aggression and the continuing threats of renewed attacks at the highest political level of the United States and the Israeli regime against Iran,” Iran said in a statement sent to member states on Wednesday.

It also cited the current US offer of a reward of up to $20 million for information on Iran’s nuclear programme.

“There is no … solid guarantee that acquired information (from inspections), that the US as a member of the Board will inevitably be informed of, would not be used for further attacks,” it added.

(Reporting by Francois Murphy; Editing by Hugh Lawson)

item.title: Binance to Remove Five Crypto Trading Pairs in 24 Hours: Countdown Begins
item.description: Binance will delist five crypto spot trading pairs within the next 24 hours on Nov. 20, 2026, following a review.To protect its users and to ensure a high-quality trading market, Binance conducts ...
item.content:encoded:
News / U.Today / Binance to Remove Five Crypto Trading Pairs in 24 Hours: Countdown Begins

Binance to Remove Five Crypto Trading Pairs in 24 Hours: Countdown Begins 1 min read

GASTRY HBARBNB HIVETRY KSMTRY Binance will delist five crypto spot trading pairs within the next 24 hours on Nov. 20, 2026, following a review. To protect its users and to ensure a high-quality trading market, Binance conducts regular reviews of all listed spot trading pairs; it may delist certain spot trading pairs for various reasons, including low liquidity and trading volume. Binance will delist GASTRY , HBARBNB , HIVETRY , KSMTRY and ZAMATRY pairs on November 20, 2026 at 03:00 UTC, according to an official announcement published on November 18. Four of the five affected pairs are related to the Turkish lira TRY , while the last one is HBARBNB . The decision affects trading between these specific assets and does not mean the cryptocurrencies themselves are being completely delisted from Binance. The exchange clarified that users will still be able to trade the affected tokens through other available spot trading pairs on its platform. Binance will terminate Spot Trading Bots services for the spot trading pairs simultaneously where applicable. Users are strongly advised to update and/or cancel their Spot Trading Bots prior to the cessation of services for Spot Trading Bots to avoid any potential losses. Binance Margin to perform routine cleanup In related news, Binance Margin will initiate a routine cleanup of Cross Margin accounts with collateral valued at less than 1 USD (or equivalent in other assets), effective from November 30, 2026 at 00:00 (UTC). The cleanup will be executed on a daily basis as an ongoing operational process. Affected accounts include Cross Margin Accounts with a collateral value of less than 1 USD equivalent across all assets and no outstanding liabilities, as well as Margin Accounts with no capital activity in the past 6 months. Capital activity refers to any action that generates a capital flow. For each eligible Small-Asset Account, the system will automatically transfer the collateral in users’ Margin Accounts to their Spot Accounts while the Margin Account functions remain normal, allowing users to transfer, borrow, or trade at any time after the cleanup. Accounts with collateral equal to or exceeding 1 USD equivalent are not affected by this cleanup.

Dollar takes a breather as investors eye Anthropic IPO

NEW YORK, Nov 19 : The dollar eased against most major peers on Thursday as its recent rally lost momentum ahead of AI company Anthropic's market debut, seen as a key test of appetite for riskier assets and broader market sentiment. The dollar rally started on November 10 when hotter-than-expected US inflation data bolstered expectations that the US Federal Reserve would tighten its policy.  Fed Governor Christopher Waller called for a more aggressive response to inflation, while minutes of the central bank's October 27 to 28 meeting showed policymakers increasingly concerned that additional tightening might be needed.  "The dollar has had a good run here ... I think a lot of good news is priced into the dollar at this point," Shaun Osborne, chief currency strategist at Scotiabank, said.

"Dollar bulls are going to need more conviction or more bullish news to drive dollar gains in the short run here," said Osborne, who pegged some of the dollar's softer tone to a pickup in risk sentiment ahead of the Anthropic IPO. Nasdaq futures rose on Thursday after Anthropic priced its IPO above the marketed range, bolstering expectations for a strong debut and reviving sentiment around AI stocks. The dollar index this week reached its highest level since April 2, 2025, when US President Donald Trump revealed a sweeping tariff package, triggering a selloff in US assets.  It was last down 0.2 per cent at 103.65, after reaching 103.97. The euro rose 0.2 per cent to $1.1002. Barclays analysts said fiscal stimulus and strong AI-related capital spending point to a resilient US economy, a wider output gap and higher-for-longer interest rates, all supportive of dollar strength. The dollar's gains have come despite a selloff in technology shares. A Deutsche Bank tracker following more than 100 foreign-domiciled exchange-traded funds showed large dip-buying of US stocks by foreigners over the last two weeks, the biggest buying spree so far this year. Such a move reinforces the view that the dollar has been supported by investor flows into US equities. YEN SLIPS AS SAFE-HAVEN FLOWS FADE The dollar was up 0.4 per cent to 159.905 yen, snapping a four-day losing streak. Analysts said that a further selloff in AI-linked assets could support the yen through safe-haven buying and repatriation flows, with the impact likely to be more pronounced against other currencies than against the dollar. The risk-sensitive Aussie was about flat on the day after hitting a fresh 11-month low earlier in the session. Australia's employment fell for a second straight month in October and the jobless rate climbed to a five-year high, bolstering the view that rates have likely peaked. "The sharp hawkish repricing of Fed rate hike expectations is contributing (to) the weakness in commodity prices and related currencies," said Lee Hardman, senior currency analyst at MUFG. UBS brought forward its forecast for the first Reserve Bank of Australia rate cut to August next year from November, and extended the easing cycle to three cuts from two, citing elevated inflation and a deterioration in the labour and housing markets. Sterling pulled back from a 20-month high against the euro, though investors remained upbeat about the UK interest rate outlook and wary of headwinds facing the single currency ahead of key elections across Europe in 2027. The pound rose 0.1 per cent against the dollar to $1.3162. In cryptocurrency markets, bitcoin rose 2.5 per cent to $63,870, pulling away from the four-month low of $62,026 touched on Sunday, aided by stronger risk appetite.

Source: Reuters

FAST

LONDON, Nov 19 : The British government has issued an order to bypass encryption to access customer data held by Apple, a London tribunal confirmed on Thursday, rejecting an argument that revealing the order's existence could damage national security. The government had said that it could not comment on the existence of the order, known as a technical capability notice, because it operated a policy of "neither confirm nor deny" on security matters. However, the Investigatory Powers Tribunal said the amount of information already in the public domain meant that confirming the order would do little, if any, damage. In response to the ruling, the British government said the right to privacy was crucial but should not come at the expense of public safety.

"Apple has been helping the police and intelligence agencies pursue criminals and bring them to justice for several years, in accordance with the law," a government spokesperson said in a statement. "This technical capability notice simply requires that they maintain the ability to do so." FIRST ORDER DROPPED AFTER US INTERVENTION In January last year, Britain issued an initial notice for what is known as a back door to allow it access to encrypted cloud backups of data of US and British citizens. That demand was dropped following months of negotiations with US President Donald Trump's administration, but in July Britain issued a second notice that applied just to Apple's UK customers. Apple launched a renewed challenge against the government at the tribunal, a specialist court, but had been unable to give public details on why because of legal restrictions. Civil rights groups and Apple had told the tribunal at a hearing in September the British government's "neither confirm nor deny" policy was an affront to open justice and prevented meaningful public discussion. The tribunal said in its ruling that the government "has not established that it would be damaging to national security to reveal in these proceedings, as is the case, that (Britain's interior ministry) has given Apple a technical capability notice." The tribunal said it had also handed down private judgments which could not be disclosed without "damaging the public interest". Thursday's ruling was merely to consider whether the notice could be publicly acknowledged and a trial to decide the substance of the case is not expected until next year. "Decisions affecting the safety of the British public must be made by democratically elected governments and independent judges, not in the boardrooms of technology companies," the government spokesperson said. UK SAID CONFIRMATION WAS RISKY The government's lawyer had argued abandoning the "neither confirm nor deny" stance posed a national security risk and would "provide material assistance to hostile actors". However, lawyers for campaign groups Privacy International and Liberty said the refusal to confirm the order's existence had become "farcical" after US politicians and officials publicly referred to the original order and unidentified UK government sources confirmed it. Akiko Hart, director of Liberty, said the ruling was "a victory for transparency". "The public deserve to know when the government's actions undermine their privacy and safety," Hart said in a statement. The tribunal said that "the extent to which, if at all, the details of the government's notice could be disclosed without damaging national security or the public interest" would be dealt with at later hearings.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 米中ロ首脳会談、「平和宣言」で合意 核戦争回避を再確認
item.description:
Jarrett Renshaw Trevor Hunnicutt
[深セン（中国） １９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Jarrett Renshaw　Trevor Hunnicutt

[深セン（中国） １９日 ロイター] - 中国の習近平国家主席、トランプ米大統領、ロシアのプーチン大統領は１９日、初の３者会談で「平和宣言」に合意、核戦争は決して起こしてはならないと再確認した。中国とロシアが明らかにした。

３首脳は宣言で、国連改革を進め、全ての国への石油製品の供給を増やすとともに、国際裁判所での国家当局者の免責特権擁護も表明した。

宣言は中国国営の新華社通信とロシア大統領府が公表した。３首脳はいずれも会談直後に声明を発表せず、トランプ氏は帰国の途に就いた。

舞台となった麒麟山荘で３首脳は円卓を囲み会談した。トランプ氏は会談冒頭、「われわれはまさに歴史をつくっている。３人で話し合うべきことは数多くある」と表明。プーチン氏は、３カ国には「ウクライナ紛争を含め、地域紛争の解決において数多くの共通の利益がある」と述べた。

トランプ氏やプーチン氏とは異なり習氏はウクライナには言及せず、「歴史が教えているのは、大国が調和し共存すれば世界は平和になり、大国が衝突すれば世界は混乱に陥るということだ」と述べた。

３カ国にはウクライナ、イラン、核兵器、貿易を巡って深い隔たりがあり、成果が得られるか疑問が残る。

トランプ氏は３者会談に先立ち、習氏、プーチン氏と個別に会談した。

麒麟山荘は、外交上重要な会合の場として長い歴史を持つ。過去には北朝鮮の故金正日総書記、習氏の父、習仲勲氏、ダライ・ラマの特使らが訪れている。

item.title: トランプ政権高官、ベネズエラへのガイアナ領土割譲提案＝関係筋
item.description:
Sarah Kinosian Gram Slattery Humeyra Pamuk
[カラカス／ワシントン １９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Sarah Kinosian　Gram Slattery　Humeyra Pamuk

[カラカス／ワシントン １９日 ロイター] - トランプ米政権高官が南米ガイアナに対し、領土の一部を隣国ベネズエラに割譲することを検討するよう持ちかけていたことが分かった。関係筋３人が明らかにした。この発言は産油国であるガイアナの当局者を驚かせ、米国は両国の国境に関する自国の政策は変わっていないとガイアナ側に保証せざるを得なくなったという。

ベネズエラは長年、ガイアナにある金、ダイヤモンド、ボーキサイトが豊富なエセキボ地域の領有権を主張してきたが、米国をはじめとする世界のほぼ全ての国はガイアナ領と認めている。

関係筋の１人によると、国務省で政策担当責任者を務めていたジェレミー・ルーウィン氏（１０月末に辞任）は９月にワシントンで行われた会談で、ガイアナのロバート・パサード外務長官に対し、ベネズエラのロドリゲス暫定大統領との領土問題に関する協議を仲介できると述べた。

他の２人の関係筋によると、ルーウィン氏はエセキボ地域をベネズエラが部分的に統治する可能性を示唆した。

ルーウィン氏はロイターとのインタビューで、ガイアナとベネズエラの領土紛争に関して、両国と「予備的な」協議を行ったと明らかにした。同氏によると、これらの協議は、ロドリゲス氏が５月にトランプ米大統領に書簡を送り、ガイアナとの領土問題に関する直接協議を促進するため、米国の仲介を求めた後に実施された。

７月にカラカスで行われた会談でロドリゲス氏からもこの問題を直接提起されたという。ルーウィン氏は、これらのやりとりはホワイトハウスによって完全に指示され、承認されたものだったと付け加えた。

このエピソードは、トランプ政権とロドリゲス暫定政権の関係が深まっていることを浮き彫りにしている。

一方、関係筋によると、ガイアナでこの出来事はエセキボ地域の地位は交渉の余地がないと繰り返し述べてきた当局者を驚かせた。

国務省当局者はコメント要請に対し、電子メールで「（同省は）外部の関係者から日々さまざまなアイデアや政策案を提示されている」ものの、ベネズエラとガイアナの国境問題に関する立場は変わっていないと回答した。

ホワイトハウスは、エセキボ地域の将来に関する協議を指示したかどうか、あるいはロドリゲス氏から書簡を受け取ったかどうかについては言及せず、国務省に問い合わせるよう求めた。

米国とベネズエラ間の関係に詳しい関係者によると、ルーウィン氏はホワイトハウスからこの問題について指示を受けていたという。

ガイアナ政府とベネズエラ政府はコメント要請に応じなかった。

item.title: 独成長率は第4四半期に加速、年明けインフレ上昇へ 連銀見通し
item.description: [フランクフルト １９日 ロイター] - ドイツ連邦銀行（中央銀行）は１９日公表した月報で、ドイツの経済成長は第４・四...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独成長率は第4四半期に加速、年明けインフレ上昇へ　連銀見通し 11/19 20:27 配信

フランクフルトの高層ビル街、10月11日撮影 REUTERS/Kai Pfaffenbach（ロイター） [フランクフルト １９日 ロイター] - ドイツ連邦銀行（中央銀行）は１９日公表した月報で、ドイツの経済成長は第４・四半期に加速する見通しだが、インフレも特に年明け以降に加速する可能性が高いと指摘した。

世界第３位の経済大国であるドイツは２６年、エネルギー価格高騰が経済に大きな打撃を与えるとの予想に反し、堅調な輸出需要と財政刺激策に支えられ、予想外に力強い成長を遂げている。

連銀によると、過去に成長の原動力だった国内消費は低迷が続くが、３年間の停滞に終止符を打った比較的堅調な景気は、今後数カ月も続く可能性が高い。「拡張的な財政政策が引き続き景気を押し上げている」とし、「産業界は国内需要の増加と世界貿易の拡大の恩恵を受けている」と説明した。

主要な予測機関の大半は現在、２６年通年のドイツの成長率が、２５年の０．３％から１％を十分に上回る水準に高まると見込んでいる。

ただ、連銀は「２７年初めにはインフレ率が急上昇すると予想される」と指摘した。

燃料補助金などの政府措置の終了だけで、インフレ率は約０．５％ポイント押し上げられる可能性がある。連銀はまた、ガス価格が上昇し、エネルギーコスト増加が他の財やサービスの価格に波及すると予想している。

１０月のインフレ率は２．９％と、ユーロ圏内で低水準だった。２７年以降の急上昇は、ユーロ圏全体のインフレ率も押し上げると見込まれている。

item.title: イスラエル軍、ガザで停戦ライン越えた戦車作戦終了
item.description:
Nidal al-Mughrabi
[カイロ １９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Nidal al-Mughrabi

[カイロ １９日 ロイター] - イスラエル軍は１９日、ガザ地区中部で、イスラム組織ハマスのものとみられるトンネルを破壊するための戦車部隊による作戦を終えたと発表した。

フェイスブックにガザ住民に向けたメッセージを投稿し、部隊が同地域での「ハマスのインフラを対象とした活動」を終了したと述べた。ガザを南北に貫く幹線道路も通行が再開されたとした。

１８日にはイスラエル軍の戦車が、イスラエルとハマスの支配地域の境界を示すイエローラインを越えた。境界線を越えて奥深くまで進攻する作戦を公表したのは、２０２５年１０月の停戦以降初めてだった。イエローライン西側にあり部隊に脅威を与えているとするトンネルを破壊するため、「標的を絞った作戦行動」を開始したと説明していた。

軍の攻撃再開を恐れたパレスチナ人の家族らは避難した。ハマスが運営するガザ政府の報道部門によると、１８日にこの地域を離れた人は約６０００人に上った。

住民らは１９日、散発的な銃声が聞こえるなど幹線道路は依然として危険で、車両も人も近づけないと語った。

LISBON, Nov 19 : Accenture said it aims to cut about 950 jobs in Portugal by January through a voluntary exit scheme for staff serving Meta Platforms, as the Facebook owner pursues an efficiency drive linked to artificial intelligence. • Accenture said it had informed teams in Lisbon providing Trust & Safety services for Meta of the plan to cut about 16 per cent of its Portugal workforce, citing "major changes in client demand for this work and our need to make significant workforce reductions" • The move comes as Meta, which owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, pursues a broader efficiency drive linked to artificial intelligence • Reuters reported in May that Meta was planning an initial round of about 8,000 job cuts globally as it ramps up AI investment

item.title: Anthropic hits US$2 trillion in Nasdaq debut, tops SpaceX's June listing
item.description: The stock opened at US$111.50, 34 per cent above its US$83 IPO price, and was last trading at US$108.72.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Business

Anthropic hits US$2 trillion in Nasdaq debut, tops SpaceX's June listing

The stock opened at US$111.50, 34 per cent above its US$83 IPO price, and was last trading at US$108.72.

CEO of Anthropic Dario Amodei, President and co-founder of Anthropic Daniela Amodei, Co-Founder and Chief Science Officer of Anthropic Jared Kaplan, Co-Founder and Head of Public Benefit of Anthropic Jack Clark celebrate as Anthropic, PBC (ANT) holds their initial public offering (IPO) at the NASDAQ MarketSite in New York City, US, Nov 19, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Brendan McDermid)

19 Nov 2026 07:07PM (Updated: 20 Nov 2026 01:39AM)

FAST

NEW YORK: Anthropic's market value hit US$2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday (Nov 19), soaring past SpaceX's massive June launch as investors rushed to buy shares of the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company. The stock opened at US$111.5, 34 per cent higher than the IPO price of US$83. It was last trading at US$108.72. The Claude chatbot maker's IPO, together with Tuesday's earnings report by AI poster child Nvidia, signals the industry has nominally passed the two big tests facing it this week. Strong demand for Anthropic shares amid a broader tech selloff offers hope to a sector where euphoria has somewhat cooled in recent weeks.

"I've looked at this whole week as a referendum on AI. Nvidia gave us a read on the buildout, and Anthropic is about to give us a read on investor appetite for the next generation of AI companies," Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion, said before the Anthropic debut. AI technology has boosted economic growth, sparked doomsday warnings and arguably helped usher in a data-centre-sceptic Democratic tsunami in the US midterm elections. Investors who once embraced the boom have turned skeptical in recent weeks over concerns that the enormous spending needed to build out the sector and the mounting debt loads may not be justified by the eventual returns. Anthropic, too, has signalled it may tap debt markets. "At some point in the future we're hoping to be investment grade, and debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future," CEO Dario Amodei told CNBC in an interview.

CEO of Anthropic Dario Amodei and President and co-founder of Anthropic Daniela Amodei celebrate as Anthropic, PBC (ANT) holds their initial public offering (IPO) at the NASDAQ MarketSite in New York City, US, Nov 19, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Brendan McDermid)

AN INDUSTRY BENCHMARK As the first frontier AI company to go public, Anthropic is poised to become the sector's benchmark, with its arch-rival OpenAI reportedly eyeing a 2027 listing. The company sold 980 million shares at US$83 each, pricing the IPO above its initial range of US$70 to US$78 set when it launched the road show. Its IPO proceeds could climb to as much as US$93.5 billion if underwriters fully exercise their option to purchase additional shares. Currently, the figure sits at over US$107 billion, including the additional US$26 billion raised through a private placement. AMD, Broadcom, Alphabet's Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC were the investors in the private placement. "Some of the demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out on the rare opportunity to gain exposure to a leading AI company, even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said. London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates passive demand from index-tracking funds will account for purchase of up to 30 per cent of Anthropic's shares offered by the end of the year. Anthropic will also join the trillion-dollar club stacked with behemoths such as Microsoft, Apple and Nvidia. The blockbuster deal is going to earn the underwriters, led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, a US$550 million fee, a regulatory filing showed.

BIG PAYDAY FOR CO-FOUNDERS Although shares can be volatile in the days following a listing, Anthropic's IPO is set to create thousands of paper millionaires and a handful of billionaires. Based on the IPO price, CEO Amodei and his six co-founders, who together own about 10 per cent of the company, had stakes valued at nearly US$150 billion combined, according to a Reuters calculation based on details in the filing. More broadly, the listing is expected to create a wave of new wealth across the AI sector, rewarding everyone from early researchers and engineers to administrative staff.

Related:

'Business as usual': Nvidia's Kress passes first test as board slams door on Huang

Commentary: Anthropic’s mega IPO is coming. Don’t let hype drive your investment decisions

JUSTIFYING THE PRICE TAG Debate has intensified across global markets in recent months over whether the AI boom is veering into bubble territory, with economists, CEOs and political leaders split over its sustainability. Much of the scrutiny has focused on circular financing arrangements. A complicated web of deals between AI companies, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors has raised questions over how much of the industry's growth is being fueled by money circulating within the same ecosystem. Anthropic's breakneck growth has so far defied these concerns, but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying. "Anthropic is a one-trick pony. People compare it with Amazon because even Amazon lost money for several years, but Anthropic won't have that luxury," said Bill Gunderson, partner at GCG Advisory Partners. "They've got to get to profitability soon." Anthropic has nearly US$900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google, underscoring how its rapid growth hinges on securing vast amounts of future computing capacity, some of which relies on financing beyond the company's control. Investors will be watching Anthropic's debut and subsequent trading closely, with analysts expecting the stock to emerge as a proxy for the broader AI trade. The company will also need to balance growth with calls to slow the development of advanced AI models. Anthropic warned in its IPO prospectus that AI could behave unpredictably and advance faster than oversight mechanisms.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: バングラデシュで暴力再燃、ハシナ氏支持者が全国的な封鎖行動
item.description: [ダッカ １９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ダッカ １９日 ロイター] - バングラデシュで１９日、ハシナ前首相の支持者が全国的な封鎖行動を実施し、新たな暴力事件が発生した。情勢が再び不安定化するとの懸念が高まっている。

これとは別に、賃上げを求める縫製労働者の抗議行動も一部の県で続いた。数百人の労働者が首都ダッカに通じる主要幹線道路を封鎖し、工場は閉鎖に追い込まれた。

ハシナ氏は２０２４年８月、学生らによるデモを受けて国外に逃れ、現在は隣国インドで亡命生活を送っている。同氏が１２月に帰国する意向を示してから、緊張が高まっている。

ハシナ氏の帰国に必要な新しい旅券（パスポート）と身分証明書の発行申請を政府が拒否したことを受け、同氏が率いるアワミ連盟は１週間にわたって抗議活動や集会を展開。その締めくくりとして、１９日に全国的な封鎖行動を呼びかけた。

警察によると、ダッカと南東部チッタゴンを結ぶ幹線道路でバス１台とトラック１台が放火された。バスの乗客は避難して無事だった。

バングラデシュ国境警備隊の報道官によると、暴力を防ぐため、ハシナ氏の支持者が多いとされるゴパルガンジとファリドプルを含む７県に９７個小隊を展開した。

＜ダッカで１０７人逮捕＞

警察の報道官によると、ダッカでは過去２４時間に、アワミ連盟やその関連組織とのつながりが疑われる１０７人を逮捕した。ナヒド元教育相も含まれる。

警察によると、チッタゴンで１８日深夜、ユヌス元暫定政権最高顧問の先祖代々の家が放火された。ハシナ氏の失脚後にバングラデシュを統治したユヌス氏とその政権は、ハシナ氏の支持者から敵視されてきた。

ラーマン政権は国外にいるアワミ連盟の指導者らが暴力をあおっていると非難し、対処すると表明した。ラーマン首相は１８日に議会で「われわれがこの国を自立したバングラデシュへと変えようとしているまさにこの時、失脚し、逃亡し、追放されたファシスト勢力がバングラデシュに対する陰謀を企て始めた」と述べた。

item.title: 韓国最高裁、戒厳令巡り韓悳洙元首相の審理差し戻し 一部判決覆す
item.description:
Heejin Kim Joyce Lee
[ソウル １９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Heejin Kim　Joyce Lee

[ソウル １９日 ロイター] - 韓国最高裁は１９日、２年前の「非常戒厳」宣言に関与したとして懲役１５年の判決を受けた韓悳洙元首相（７７）について、一部の判決を覆し、審理を高裁に差し戻した。

韓被告が戒厳令発令に正当性を与える意図で閣議を手配したとする二審の認定に異議を唱えた。ただ、戒厳令発令後、同被告が関連文書への閣僚の署名を求めるなどの行動を通じて「憲法秩序を転覆させる」意図を示したとする二審の判断については同意した。

特別検察チームは声明で、裁判所の判決を尊重すると述べた。

韓被告は、偽証罪の１件を除く全ての罪状を否認している。

最高裁はまた、尹錫悦前大統領の妻で、株式取引不正や、韓国の統一教会からの賄賂受領で有罪判決を受けていた金建希被告に対する懲役４年の判決を支持した。

item.title: デンマーク議会、グリーンランド巡る対米協定を全会一致で批准
item.description:
Stine Jacobsen Tom Little
[コペンハーゲン １９日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Stine Jacobsen　Tom Little

[コペンハーゲン １９日 ロイター] - デンマーク議会は１９日、グリーンランドを巡るトランプ米大統領との安全保障協定を全会一致で批准した。米欧関係を揺るがしてきたグリーンランドの将来を巡る対立に終止符を打ちたい考えだ。

米国、デンマーク、グリーンランド自治政府は９月、緊張の解消に向けて協定に署名した。鉱物資源が豊富なグリーンランドは人口５万７０００人のデンマーク自治領で、トランプ氏は同島を支配下に置くと繰り返し威嚇していた。

ルビオ米国務長官はＸに投稿した声明で「この協定は米国、デンマーク、グリーンランドの防衛パートナーシップを近代化し、米国と北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）の同盟国の国家安全保障を強化するものだ」と表明した。

この協定は行政協定で米上院の採決は必要ない。デンマーク議会での採決を受け、同国外務省が手続きの完了を外交文書で米国に通知すれば発効する。グリーンランド議会は１１月に協定を批准している。

協定はグリーンランドでの米軍の役割を広げ、ミサイル防衛システム「ゴールデンドーム」の構築も認める。一方で、デンマークの主権とグリーンランド住民の自決権を改めて確認している。

コペンハーゲン大学のミケル・ベズビュー・ラスムセン教授（政治学）は「これが終わりではなく、むしろ始まりだと示す兆候が数多くある」と述べた。「米国はこの条約を根拠に、安全保障政策に関わる意思決定や、一部の戦略資源の採掘について、より大きな影響力を求めることができる」と指摘した。

これに対し、新協定によって米軍のグリーンランド利用が大きく拡大するわけではないとみる専門家もいる。同島は欧州から北米への最短ルート上に位置しており、最北端の米軍基地は既にグリーンランドにあるためだ。

item.title: US Fed warns of fin stability risks from AI boom and elevated asset valuations
item.description: The US Federal Reserve has flagged financial stability risks from the AI investment boom, elevated asset valuations and rising hedge fund leverage. Policymakers warned that disappointing returns on AI investments, heavy borrowing and concentrated market exposure could trigger broader financial disruptions, even as banks and households remain relatively resilient.
item.dc:creator: Anupam Nagar
item.content:encoded: The US Federal Reserve is monitoring financial stability risks stemming from aggressive investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and elevated asset valuations, as policymakers warned that disappointing returns from the technology boom could trigger broader financial market disruptions, Reuters reported.Minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 policy meeting, released on Wednesday, showed that officials were concerned about the potential consequences of heavy AI-related borrowing, rising leverage among hedge funds and concentrated exposure to a small number of companies.According to Reuters, Fed policymakers and central bank staff raised these concerns as part of a broader assessment of vulnerabilities in the financial system. The review found that elevated asset valuations and hedge fund leverage were among the most significant sources of risk, although strong balance sheets among banks and households offered some protection against severe financial shocks.Read more: South Korean shares fall over 1% as hawkish Fed remarks weigh on sentimentPolicymakers were particularly concerned about the possibility that returns on AI investments could fall short of investor expectations. The minutes highlighted the rapid growth of AI-related debt, much of which has been channelled through complex and relatively opaque financing structures, Reuters reported.Some officials also flagged the concentration of AI exposure among a limited number of companies, raising concerns that setbacks involving major players could have wider consequences for financial markets and the economy.Hedge funds emerged as another area of concern, with policymakers identifying high leverage and limited capacity among financial dealers to intermediate transactions as potential channels through which market stress could intensify, Reuters reported,Although Fed staff described the financial system as resilient and noted that banks had ample access to liquidity, some policymakers cautioned that vulnerabilities within the banking sector could emerge rapidly despite initially reassuring assessments. Officials also questioned whether existing regulatory data fully captured the extent of financial institutions' exposure to potential risks.Read more: Japan stocks fall as metal shares slide; investors await Anthropic IPO debutFed weighs measures to strengthen financial resilienceThe minutes also revealed discussions among policymakers about measures to improve the financial system's ability to withstand future disruptions.A few officials considered increasing capital requirements for banks, while others emphasised the importance of ensuring that lenders were better prepared to access the Fed's emergency lending discount window during periods of market stress.Some policymakers also discussed the possibility of creating a dedicated asset-purchasing mechanism aimed specifically at addressing financial stability risks.The debate comes as the Federal Reserve reassesses how it uses its balance sheet as a policy tool. Its holdings expanded significantly following large-scale bond-buying programmes introduced during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.According to Reuters, the pandemic-era bond purchases initially designed to stabilise markets eventually evolved into a broader monetary stimulus programme, highlighting the challenges of distinguishing between emergency market support and conventional monetary easing.Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack has advocated a more clearly defined framework for such interventions, including an exit strategy to unwind bond holdings once financial stability has been restored. She has argued that any asset-purchasing programme should be temporary, with holdings sold in a timely manner after market conditions normalise, Reuters reported.Several policymakers, however, cautioned against relying on monetary policy to address financial market disruptions, suggesting that other tools may be more appropriate for containing emerging vulnerabilities.The minutes also showed that almost all Fed policymakers believed further interest rate increases could be necessary if the economy developed in line with their expectations. Officials had kept interest rates unchanged at the October meeting amid persistent inflation concerns.The growing importance of AI and technology investment in driving economic growth could complicate the Fed's policy decisions if a significant correction in the sector were to threaten broader financial stability.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.description: [ベルリン １９日 ロイター] - ドイツ当局は、エージェント型ＡＩ（人工知能）システムが攻撃者にさらなる機会を提供し...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ドイツ当局、ＩＴセキュリティー脅威評価上げ　「緊迫から危機的」 11/19 18:50 配信

11月4日、ベルリンのドイツ連邦議会。REUTERS/Fabrizio Bensch（ロイター） [ベルリン １９日 ロイター] - ドイツ当局は、エージェント型ＡＩ（人工知能）システムが攻撃者にさらなる機会を提供していると指摘し、情報技術（ＩＴ）システムに対する脅威の評価を「緊迫から危機的」へと引き上げた。

連邦情報セキュリティー庁（ＢＳＩ）が１９日に発表した報告書によると、多くの企業や消費者は、自らが直面しているリスクについて誤った安心感を抱いていたという。

同庁は年に一度、脅威評価を発表している。昨年は状況を「緊迫」と表現していた。

報告書は「かつては脆弱性の悪用に専門知識が必要で、ある程度の時間を要していたが、攻撃はますます迅速化し、低コスト化が進み、標的を絞ったものになっている」と指摘。高性能なＡＩモデルは、ますます高速かつ広範囲にわたり弱点を発見・悪用できるようになっており、この脅威は現時点で「重大な局面」を迎えていると述べた。

また、政府がＩＴセキュリティー規制の強化において進展を見せている一方で、多くの企業が防御体制の強化に遅れをとっており、特に攻撃前にＡＩシステムを活用して脆弱性をスキャンできていないと分析した。

「中小企業はドイツ経済の屋台骨をなしているが、攻撃に対抗する手段がほとんどない場合が多い」と報告書は述べた。重要インフラの運営事業者は概して保護体制が整っているものの、「改善の余地がある」とも付け加えた。

item.title: Walmart lifts annual forecasts, flags $2 bn fuel and transport cost burden
item.description: Walmart raised its fiscal 2027 sales and earnings forecasts, but warned that higher diesel and transportation costs have added about $2 billion to expenses this year.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Walmart lifts annual forecasts, flags $2 bn fuel and transport cost burden

Walmart lifts annual forecasts, flags $2 bn fuel and transport cost burden Walmart raised its fiscal 2027 sales and earnings forecasts, but warned that higher diesel and transportation costs have added about $2 billion to expenses this year.

Walmart has raised its annual forecasts on strong e-commerce and membership growth, while warning that higher fuel and transportation expenses are adding pressure to costs ahead of the holiday shopping season. (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 19 2026 | 11:20 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Rising fuel costs are complicating Walmart's efforts to keep prices low even as strong growth in its delivery and membership businesses prompted the retailer to raise annual forecasts ahead of the crucial holiday shopping season. The world's largest retailer, seen as a bellwether for US consumer health, reported a 5.2% rise in third-quarter revenue to $188.84 billion, beating expectations. It now expects fiscal 2027 net sales to grow 4.9% to 5.2%, up from its previous forecast of 4% to 5%, but still below analysts' expectations for growth of 5.5%, according to data compiled by LSEG. CEO John Furner said surging diesel and transportation costs had added about $2 billion in incremental expenses this year and could hamper efforts to keep prices low as consumers head into the holiday shopping season.

"We will do everything we can in terms of efficiency," Furner said on a post-earnings call, adding that pricing "really depends on transportation costs and input costs as we move forward." Also Read

Nifty tops 25,500 for first time since February; Sensex reclaims 83K

Hind Copper, SAIL, NMDC among 6 stocks on analysts radar amid metals slide

Silver ETF, Suzlon, TFCI among top traded mid-, small-caps under MTF in Nov

Extended market hours not a priority for India, says Sebi Chairman

Markets decline over 0.6% as metals, consumer durables fall behind

HOLIDAY PLANS Walmart has cut prices on thousands of grocery and general merchandise items this year as Americans seek cheaper options amid high inflation and an Iran War that has pushed up fuel prices. Consumer sentiment, while improving in November, remains weak. Rising freight and logistics costs have squeezed profits across the retail and consumer goods industries, though Walmart has partly offset the impact through nearly $3 billion in tariff refunds, Furner said.

Still, executives struck an upbeat tone about the holiday shopping season. "It's game time," Furner said, noting that Walmart had sold 1 million more Thanksgiving turkeys than a year earlier after cutting the price of its holiday meal basket to its lowest since the programme was launched in 2022. The retailer has leaned on its stores as "digital fulfilment nodes" for e-commerce orders and its higher-margin third-party marketplace, which posted gains during the quarter. That has helped support sales as growth in store visits has slowed from a year earlier. "The margin story is outrunning the traffic story right now," said David Wagner, head of equity at Aptus Capital Advisors.

The retailer has pushed deeper into membership, e-commerce and marketplace businesses to diversify revenue and support margins. Last month, it launched a bundled membership offer for its Walmart+ loyalty programme and its Sam's Club wholesale unit. Membership fee revenue rose by double digits in the three months through October. Its push into faster delivery has also helped drive repeat purchases, while customers using the service were more likely to sign up for its membership programme, the company said. Overall, US e-commerce sales increased 23%, compared with 28% growth a year earlier. Walmart raised its annual adjusted earnings forecast to $2.84 to $2.89 per share from $2.80 to $2.87 previously. Analysts expect $2.88 per share.

Adjusted earnings of 65 cents per share edged past estimates, while operating expenses rose 5% to $40.01 billion. Walmart shares fell about 2%. The stock has gained about 14% this year and is on track for a fourth straight annual gain.

Cartesi @cartesiproject

Review the details and cast your vote here: https://t.co/qfaEWpIK5k Voting period 🗓ï¸ Nov 18 - Nov 25 pic.twitter.com/EywpwXewyy

CTSI Info Cartesi (CTSI) is a blockchain project aiming to make the development and deployment of decentralized applications (DApps) more practical and scalable. It does this by enabling smart contracts to run off-chain computations in a Linux environment, which opens up the possibility to use mainstream programming languages and software, as well as access larger amounts of data more efficiently. The fundamental piece of technology behind Cartesi is the Descartes SDK, a software development kit that provides a set of tools and services to help developers build scalable and secure DApps. With Descartes, computations can be intensive and incorporate complex business logic as they are executed off-chain in a Linux environment. The Cartesi token (CTSI) serves multiple utility purposes within the Cartesi ecosystem. It is used as a staking mechanism in the network's Proof-of-Stake (PoS) consensus algorithm, and also as a means to pay for computational resources within the network. In addition, it's used in the network's incentive system for data availability and computation verification.

item.title: GTA VI wins rave reviews as gamers enter Vice City after 13-year wait
item.description: After 13 years in the making, GTA VI has launched worldwide to strong early reviews, with Sensor Tower estimating sales of over 17 million copies worth more than $1.65 billion.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / GTA VI wins rave reviews as gamers enter Vice City after 13-year wait

GTA VI wins rave reviews as gamers enter Vice City after 13-year wait After 13 years in the making, GTA VI has launched worldwide to strong early reviews, with Sensor Tower estimating sales of over 17 million copies worth more than $1.65 billion.

Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI has launched worldwide after a 13-year wait, drawing strong early reviews and significant player interest as the latest instalment in one of the world's best-selling video game franchises. (Screenshot)

Reuters 5 min read Last Updated : Nov 19 2026 | 11:12 PM IST

Listen to This Article

After 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, "Grand Theft Auto VI" rolled out across the globe on Thursday, gaining rapturous early reviews for the most anticipated video game release in history. The game, which could bring in billions of dollars for its developer, Take-Two Interactive studio Rockstar Games, raced to the top of Metacritic's all-time gaming leaderboard with a score of 99, a mark matched by only one other title, Nintendo's 1998 classic "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time". The rollout began as the clock struck midnight in New Zealand and moved across time zones from Tokyo to Miami, prompting launch parties, posts from world leaders and even some companies giving staff the day off to play.

"It is the best game that's ever been made and we're only 20 minutes deep," said 33-year-old Asif Mir as he started to play and livestream just after midnight in Sydney. In London, gamers counted down to the release at parties across the city. Also Read

Gamers skip work, crowd gaming cafes for GTA VI as PM Modi joins the buzz

Grand Theft Auto 6: New Vice City, record viewership, and global frenzy

Get GTA 6 in minutes: Blinkit rolls out quick delivery in 11 cities

Grand Theft Auto VI wins rave reviews as gamers return to Vice City

GTA 6 India launch: First impressions, prices, editions and download size

"Today has been a day that I have waited for my whole life," said 20-year-old influencer Archie Whitby. "To be living it, it feels almost dystopian. It doesn't feel real." Miami, the inspiration for the game's fictional Vice City setting, was one of the last places to get in on the action. The city's NBA team, the Miami Heat, celebrated with a Vice City-themed match against the Milwaukee Bucks, with the court and stadium adorned with the game's colours of neon pink and blue.

Mia Pazan travelled to Miami for the launch. "I came here, number one, because I love GTA VI. I played literally all the games," she said, adding that as a Latina woman she loved the fact that there was a protagonist — co-lead character Lucia Caminos — reflecting her identity. "I really identify with Lucia a lot," she added. Millions of players have already downloaded the game to their consoles, with many taking time off work — or calling in sick — to play the latest instalment in a franchise that since its 1997 debut has become one of the best-selling video game series of all time.

"It's the Star Wars of this generation," said Joost van Dreunen, adjunct professor at NYU Stern School of Business. "It's a synchronized, shared event. So millions of people will all want to be there the first couple of days, the first few weeks of experiencing it as it goes live." Strong initial reviews of the game — available on Sony's PlayStation 5 and Microsoft's Xbox Series X and S consoles — helped push Take-Two Interactive's US shares higher on Wednesday. GREAT STRESS RELIEF' FOR FEMALE GAMERS The original "Grand Theft Auto" looks basic by today's standards, with a storyline — stealing cars and carrying out jobs for crime syndicates — that angered politicians and parents, even as it delighted fans.

But as the series progressed it became increasingly sophisticated, mixing its trademark crime, driving and morally dubious missions with activities ranging from parachute jumps to cinema visits and radio stations satirising US culture. "Grand Theft Auto V", released in 2013, was set in the fictional Los Santos, a stand-in for Los Angeles. The action now moves to Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, in the state of Leonida, the game's take on Florida. Play will switch between two leading characters, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval. They are partners in crime and romantically involved — just how romantically will be up to the player. There will be nightclubs, gun stores, scuba diving and a zoo. But much remains to be revealed.

GTA VI could prove less provocative than its predecessors, said Tore Olsson, a professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville. "There's no doubt that Jason and Lucia of VI will be criminals, and they'll be regularly breaking the law," said Olsson. "But I don't think the new game will require players to enact wanton slaughter, and it may indeed penalize those who choose to play that way." Having Lucia as a lead character should help address complaints about a lack of playable female characters in previous iterations of GTA. Women will be an estimated four out of 10 GTA VI players in the US, according to a Bain survey.

"Since you can do all that brutal stuff like running people over or hitting them, my first thought was that it's mostly for male players," said 30-year-old Tokyo worker Suzana Onoda. "After trying it out, well, I think getting to beat people up is a great stress relief for women as well." STRONG REVIEWS: 'TRULY ASTONISHING', 'A MASTERPIECE' Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimated that more than 17 million copies had been sold so far for over $1.65 billion. With the main part of the game estimated to take around 50 hours to complete, full reactions were not available immediately. But initial reviews from gaming industry experts were almost universal in their high praise.

Entertainment website GamesRadar+ said Rockstar had built a world of "truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality". The release "will be talked about for years to come" and was "well worth the 13-year wait", said PC Games. Various outlets called it a "masterpiece". While some economists have warned about lost productivity as gamers take time off from work, consumer analysts said the economy could also receive a boost from sales of the game, consoles, storage upgrades and even food delivery services. In India, home to hundreds of millions of gamers, Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted Grand Theft Auto-inspired social media content and some firms gave employees the day off.

On Australia's southern island of Tasmania, family-run fragrance shop Whiff-it! will close for a week after 20-year-old Jonah Bowen-Brown persuaded his mother to give him and his brother time off to play. "She was really against it at first," said Bowen-Brown. "I had to say, mum, please, please, I need it... I've been waiting 13 years to play the game."

item.title: US STOCKS-Wall St falls sharply as Anthropic debut fails to reignite AI trade
item.description: US stock indexes tumbled on Thursday after Anthropic's blockbuster market debut did little to alleviate concerns over the AI trade. Shares of the AI lab briefly soared past $2 trillion in market ...
item.content:encoded:
US STOCKS-Wall St falls sharply as Anthropic debut fails to reignite AI trade Reuters | Updated: 19-11-2026 23:07 IST | Created: 19-11-2026 23:07 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US stock indexes tumbled on Thursday after Anthropic's blockbuster market debut did little to alleviate concerns over the AI trade. Shares of the AI lab briefly soared past $2 trillion in market valuation before easing to $1.78 trillion. The company priced its upsized offering at $83 per share on Wednesday, above its marketed range of $70 to $78, raising $81 billion in the largest listing on record. "It has failed to rekindle enthusiasm for tech stocks. We wouldn’t read too much into the expected initial 'pop' in Anthropic’s share price as a stock’s early trading tends to be noisy," said Joe Maher, market economist, Capital Economics, London. "But how it fares in the coming months will be a key litmus test for investors’ enthusiasm." The listing follows weeks of selling in chipmakers and cloud companies as investors fretted over stretched valuations, heavy spending on AI infrastructure and the fallout from the abrupt exit of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Amazon fell 0.8%, while Alphabet was slightly higher. Both are among the biggest investors in the AI lab. Advanced Micro Devices shares tumbled 10% after investigative outlet Hunterbrook said its affiliated fund, Hunterbrook Capital, had taken a short position in the company. Most tech stocks were lower, with Micron and Broadcom down between 1% and 3%. Nvidia declined 0.5% after five straight sessions of losses through Wednesday, when its upbeat revenue forecast did little to lift sentiment. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dipped 0.2%. Neocloud firms CoreWeave and Nebius were down 1.2% and 4.4%, respectively. The broader technology sector was down 1.4%. At 12:18 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,022.85 points, or 2.03%, to 49,180.77, the S&P 500 lost 118.60 points, or 1.59%, to 7,207.35 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 384.25 points, or 1.55%, to 24,051.46.

The Pit is heating up. Privacy is taking center stage. 🎙ï¸ SKALE Spotlight Episode 3 is breaking down the AgentPit Kickoff Clash and diving deep into Programmable Privacy. Join @iFalcore , @oibaftom , @dmtkatwork & @rikon_azane live tomorrow 8am PT! pic.twitter.com/SjHfK0U4Xi

SKL Info SKALE is a high-throughput, gas-free network of interconnected, modular blockchains. Designed to enhance Ethereum projects, it provides a scalable environment for developers to shift their projects from Ethereum, achieving better performance. Operating in tandem with Ethereum, SKALE leverages its unique consensus mechanism. It effectively marries Ethereum’s proof-of-stake (PoS) framework with SKALE’s pooled security model. This synergy results in secure, rapid transactions devoid of gas fees, positioning SKALE as an efficient platform, particularly for Web3 and gaming applications, enhancing Ethereum’s scalability for wider adoption. SKL, the utility token of SKALE, is an ERC-777 token, maintaining backward compatibility with the ERC-20 standard. Offering token-level delegation, it enables non-custodial staking directly from user wallets, bypassing traditional smart contract locks. Within the network, SKL finds its use in payments, especially for SKALE chain subscriptions. Token holders, be it as validators or delegators, can stake SKL to earn rewards. Validators, by running nodes, ensure the network's security, transaction validation, and smart contract execution, earning SKL in return. Delegators, while playing a passive role, earn a fraction of these rewards.

The new features are live on https://t.co/BX9xgM9Tt3 and the Enjin Platform, and a new version of Enjinâ€¦ pic.twitter.com/wfNAoMXuzN

Nov 17, 2026

ENJ Info Enjin is a comprehensive platform designed around the intersection of blockchain and gaming. Spearheaded by Enjin, this ecosystem offers a suite of interconnected gaming products with the Enjin Network at its core, where users engage in social gaming activities, including the creation of gaming websites, clans, chat forums, and virtual item storefronts. Central to Enjin’s functionality is its ability to let developers tokenize in-game items on the Ethereum blockchain. Through this mechanism, real-world value is imparted to these digital assets, enabling their purchase, sale, and trade on integrated marketplaces. This digitization process does more than just virtualize items; it brings transparency, verifies authenticity, and guarantees the scarcity of the tokenized assets, enhancing their inherent value and utility across various applications. Serving as the backbone of the Enjin ecosystem is the Enjin Coin (ENJ), an ERC-20 token. This digital store of value is integral to the creation and backing of blockchain assets, especially non-fungible tokens (NFTs). Every NFT produced within the Enjin platform has ENJ embedded within it, effectively locking this value and removing the corresponding ENJ from the general circulation. This system not only ensures that the assets possess inherent value but also provides liquidity and introduces an anti-inflationary model. Furthermore, Enjin’s distinctive “melting” feature grants users the option to dissolve their assets, subsequently reclaiming the intrinsic ENJ.

FAST

BRUSSELS, Nov 19 : The European Commission confirmed on Thursday that it was targeted by a cyberattack through the use of AI tools, although it said that it was difficult to judge the scale of the incident given that an inquiry was underway. "I can confirm that the Commission has recently taken necessary steps in response to a detected cybercampaign," European Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said at a press briefing.  "As a protective and preventive measure, we temporarily took down several applications and most of them have since been restored," he added. "The investigation is still ongoing. We are taking any necessary steps, based on the findings as they come." "This was an AI-generated cybercampaign," said Regnier.

The incident was detected on October 22 and there was no evidence of any data breach affecting Commission staff as a whole, Regnier said. He declined to say who the Commission thought was behind the attack, and said he was not aware of any ransom demand following the incident. The attack on the Commission is the latest high-profile cyberattack, after hacks knocked out commercial refrigerators and freezers in hundreds of French supermarkets in October, ships bound for the United States in August, US water treatment plants in July and the Los Angeles transit system in March.  Separately, an hourslong nationwide ground stop in the United States and outages to banking and Microsoft applications were blamed by tech experts on attempts to rapidly patch newly identified software vulnerabilities.  Politico reported earlier on Thursday that the Commission was targeted by a cyberattack which might have compromised large amounts of personal data, with several systems, including HR systems for payslips and time management and a system for medical reimbursements, taken offline during the 10-day disruption. The Commission convened its highest-level internal crisis management body for an urgent meeting about the cyber incidents and tech commissioner Henna Virkkunen briefed other commissioners on Wednesday, according to Politico. Virkkunen's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝香港株4カ月ぶり安値 中国も軟調 米中貿易摩擦が再燃
item.description: ［１９日 ロイター］ - 香港株式市場ではハンセン指数が２％下落し、６月下旬以来の安値を付けた。中国株も下押し圧力にさ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝香港株4カ月ぶり安値　中国も軟調　米中貿易摩擦が再燃 11/19 18:27 配信

［１９日　ロイター］ - 香港株式市場ではハンセン指数が２％下落し、６月下旬以来の安値を付けた。中国株も下押し圧力にさらされた。中国の習近平国家主席とトランプ米大統領が深センで会談したにもかかわらず、米中間の貿易摩擦が再燃した。

米国の追加利上げで世界的に流動性が引き締まるとの見方も、投資家のリスク選好を冷やした。

ハンセンテック指数は７営業日続落し、２６カ月ぶりの安値となった。

中国本土市場では、ＣＳＩ３００指数が横ばいで取引を終えた。上海総合指数は０．３％下落し、１５カ月超ぶりの安値を付けた。

習氏は１９日、トランプ氏と協力し、両国関係を「正しい軌道」に導く方針を堅持すると述べた。一方、中国商務省は、米国が最近相次いで打ち出した対中経済・貿易制限措置に強く反対する姿勢を示した。

香港上場のＡＩモデル開発企業や人工知能（ＡＩ）向け大規模クラウド事業者の株価は急落した。ミニマックス（稀宇科技）は一時１１％下落し、過去最安値を付けた。Ｚ．ＡＩは２％下落した。

騰訊控股（テンセント）は７％近く下落し、３１カ月ぶりの安値となった。アリババは５．５％下落し、２２カ月ぶりの安値を付けた。上海天数智芯半導体は１７％下落した。

中国市場では、クラウドコンピューティング、ＡＩ、ビッグデータなど、先端半導体に依存するハイテク株が下げを主導した。

ロイター 関連リンク アングル：米の対中抑止後退に警戒感、日本政府・与党　習氏は高市氏批判も 焦点：米中首脳会談、市場は両国関係安定に期待　イラン紛争は進展なく失望 アングル：成果乏しい首脳会談、米中関係は「脆弱な休戦」に回帰 焦点：米中会談、日本政府・与党内に歓迎と警戒　台湾問題「厳しい時代」との声も 焦点：ＡＩ企業がシンガポールに相次ぎ拠点、米中対立の「中立地帯」に 11/19(木) 18:27 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: 米中ロ首脳、初の３者会談開始 核軍縮やウクライナ協議へ
item.description:
Jarrett Renshaw Trevor Hunnicutt
［深セン（中国） １９日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Jarrett Renshaw　Trevor Hunnicutt

［深セン（中国）　１９日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領、中国の習近平国家主席、ロシアのプーチン大統領は１９日、初の３者での首脳会談を開始した。ウクライナ戦争や核軍備管理について協議するとしている。

円卓を囲む会合で３首脳は順に冒頭発言を行った。

トランプ氏は「われわれはまさに歴史をつくっている。３人で話し合うべきことは数多くある」と表明。「対話の機会を拒むことで平和が築かれたことは一度もない」と語った。

プーチン氏は、３カ国には「ウクライナ紛争を含め、地域紛争の解決において数多くの共通の利益がある」と述べた。

中国国営メディアによると習氏が議長を務める。トランプ氏やプーチン氏とは異なり習氏はウクライナには言及せず、「歴史が教えているのは、大国が調和し共存すれば世界は平和になり、大国が衝突すれば世界は混乱に陥るということだ」と述べた。

中国国営の新華社通信によると、習氏は、核兵器のない世界の構築を最終目標に、核兵器を全面的に禁止し、完全に廃棄すべきだと表明。核戦争に勝者はなく、決して起こしてはならないとし、核戦争防止にあらゆる努力を尽くすべきだと述べた。

ロシアの通信社によると、プーチン氏は３カ国が建設的に協力すれば世界の安定を強化できるとし、世界や地域の諸問題に加え、エネルギー安全保障について協議する意向を示した。

item.description: ANTALYA, Turkey Nov 19 : Venezuela is using artificial intelligence to make its oil and gas industry more efficient and curb its environmental footprint, part of a strategy to expand fossil fuel production rather than phase it out, the country's new vice minister for AI and hydrocarbons told Reuters."Our poli

At COP31, Venezuela touts AI as path to cleaner oil production

FILE PHOTO: An oil pumpjack at Lake Maracaibo, in Cabimas, Venezuela, January 27, 2026. REUTERS/Leonardo Fernandez Viloria/File Photo

19 Nov 2026 04:56PM (Updated: 19 Nov 2026 04:58PM)

FAST

ANTALYA, Turkey Nov 19 : Venezuela is using artificial intelligence to make its oil and gas industry more efficient and curb its environmental footprint, part of a strategy to expand fossil fuel production rather than phase it out, the country's new vice minister for AI and hydrocarbons told Reuters. "Our policy is not to stop producing hydrocarbons," Albania del Mar Villarroel Gomez said on the sidelines of the COP31 climate summit in Antalya. "Our goal is to reduce waste and emissions while maintaining energy production." Villarroel said Venezuela is using AI to monitor emissions and methane leaks and improve oilfield operations, reflecting the country's argument at the UN climate talks that technology can help reconcile continued fossil fuel production with efforts to limit its environmental impact. Venezuela's oil and gas sector is among the world's most polluting. Its upstream methane emissions intensity is nearly six times the global average, according to the International Energy Agency. It is the only major energy producer in Central and South America that has not signed the Global Methane Pledge.
